transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because I feel worn down almost all the time. Even if I sleep through the night, I don’t really feel rested, and after getting through work and dealing with the clutter at home, I just don’t have much left for anything else.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I think so. Most days there’s this kind of low, gray mood in the background. I can still go to the lab and talk to people, but I don’t really feel much excitement about things I used to enjoy, like baking or checking the telescope. It just feels flatter than it used to.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even about everyday things?
I’m not sure I’d say I worry a lot. I mean, I think about normal stuff—work, chores, things I need to get done—but I haven’t really noticed it being the main problem.
How has your appetite been lately?
I haven’t really been paying close attention to it. I think my appetite is mostly normal—nothing that’s stood out to me lately.
Did these feelings start after a particular stressful event or major life change?

I think it started not long after we moved into the older house. That was a little over two years ago. I don’t know if I’d call it one big event exactly, but that’s when this low baseline seemed to settle in.
Since this started, have you felt this low and flat most days for the past two years?

Yes… most days it’s there. It’s like a low, gray mood in the background. I can still go to the lab and talk to people and get through things, but I don’t really feel light or excited about stuff I used to enjoy, like baking or checking the telescope.
During the past two years, has there been any stretch of two months or longer when your mood felt back to normal?

No, I don’t think so. Since shortly after we moved into that older house, a little over two years ago, it’s been pretty consistently there as my baseline. I might have better days, but not two months where I felt normal again.
During this time, have you had any period when your depression became much worse than your usual baseline for at least two weeks?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think there’s been a clear two-week stretch where it got a lot worse than usual. It’s more been this steady low feeling, with some days worse than others, but nothing that stands out like a separate episode.
Over the past two years, have you often had trouble sleeping?
I’m not sure I’d say often. My sleep hasn’t really stood out to me as a major problem. Some nights are off, but I haven’t been keeping track or noticed a clear pattern.
Do you often feel low on energy?

Yes. I feel worn down most of the time, even if I’ve slept through the night. By the time I get through work and then deal with the house and the clutter, I don’t have much energy left for anything else.
Do you often feel hopeless?

Yes, I do. I catch myself thinking the house is never really going to feel settled, and that I’m probably just going to keep functioning at this lower level. It makes it hard to plan things ahead, like trips or even stargazing projects I used to look forward to.
Do you often feel bad about yourself?
I don’t know that I’d say often. I get frustrated with myself sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed a constant feeling of being bad about who I am.
Do you often have trouble concentrating?

Yes, I do. Things that used to feel pretty straightforward, like revising a grant paragraph or deciding what materials to buy for a home repair, take me longer now. My mind just feels slower, and I catch myself second-guessing small decisions.
Have these symptoms made it hard for you to function in your daily life?

Yes, somewhat. I’m still getting my lab work done, so it’s not like I’ve stopped functioning, but grant drafts and routine project decisions take noticeably longer than they used to. And at home, I’ve kind of dropped the baking, the bonsai, and the telescope plans that used to give my downtime some structure.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living?
No, not really. I’ve been discouraged and tired of dealing with things sometimes, but I don’t think I’ve had thoughts that life isn’t worth living.
When you wake up in the morning, do you usually feel refreshed?

Not usually, no. Even if I’ve slept through the night, I still wake up feeling worn down. It’s like I start the day already low on energy, and after work and dealing with the house, there isn’t much left.
Has anyone ever told you that you snore loudly?
I’m not really sure. No one’s mentioned loud snoring to me, at least not that I can remember.
Even when you’re away from the house for a few days, does the low gray mood still stay with you?

Yeah, it does. Being away from the house might make things a little less stressful, but that low, gray mood is still kind of there in the background most days. I can still do things and talk to people, but I don’t really feel light or excited about things the way I used to.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energized or high, needing much less sleep than usual?
No, I don’t think so. I can’t remember a time where I felt unusually high or energized and didn’t need much sleep. If anything, I usually feel more tired than anything.
Do you wake up much earlier than you want to and then have trouble getting back to sleep?
I’m not sure. I don’t really keep track of the exact time I wake up. I haven’t noticed a pattern of waking up way too early and then being stuck awake, though.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a chronic depressed mood present most days for over two years, without any symptom-free period longer than two months, and without a distinct major depressive episode. Confirmed associated symptoms include low energy, hopelessness, poor concentration/indecisiveness, and reduced interest/pleasure, with mild but clear functional impairment. This pattern is most consistent with persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) rather than episodic major depression, adjustment disorder, or a primary sleep disorder.
